title: Unified Inference: Q4 2027 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document consolidates the Q4 2027 product overview, PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference — the unified runtime and developer experience for running LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and documentation teams to coordinate roadmap priorities and external messaging for the upcoming release window.

Goals (Q4 2027)

- Deliver predictable latency & cost improvements for medium and high-concurrency workloads (target: 20-35% token-cost reduction for typical web chat workloads).
- Launch unified pricing tiers and clearer packaging for cross-environment customers.
- Harden canary and rollback tooling for Dedicated & Private deployments; reduce customer rollback time to <30 minutes median.
- Expand model routing policies with cost-aware fallbacks and region-aware routing.

Scope

Included:
- Product work for API surface, SDK updates, pricing pages, and console UX.
- Runtime optimizations (kernel tuning, batching profiles, prefix cache improvements).
- Rollout tooling (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and Dedicated autoscaling policy changes.
- Documentation, release notes, and sales enablement artifacts.

Excluded:
- Large model training workflows or model development tooling.
- Major data residency legal changes (handled separately by Security & Legal).

User Stories and Requirements (PRD)

1) Developer: Self-serve migration to new pricing and SDK features
- Requirement: Upgrade path for existing API keys that preserves existing usage tiers for 90 days.
- Acceptance criteria: 95% of migrated accounts see unchanged monthly invoices within tolerance (±15%) or are surfaced with a migration recommendation.

2) Platform engineer: Predictable high-throughput inference for Dedicated pools
- Requirement: Dedicated autoscaling responds within 120s to sustained +30% load for 5 minutes; burst capacity available for 60s at 2x baseline.
- Acceptance criteria: Measured on synthetic load tests; 99th percentile response below configured latency SLO with <1% error rate.

3) SRE: Faster rollbacks with safe fallback to compatible model variants
- Requirement: Canary deploys must be able to automatically rollback to last-good model within 5 minutes of a health policy breach.
- Acceptance criteria: Simulated canary failures result in successful rollback and traffic rejoin within 5 minutes in 95% of runs.

Non-functional requirements

- Latency SLOs (hosted): p50 <= 120ms for short inputs (<= 128 tokens); p95 <= 450ms.
- Availability: 99.95% per month for hosted API endpoints.
- Security: All Private deployments must pass KMS integration validation and audit-logging enabled by default.
- Observability: Token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency histograms available in Console within 5 minutes of ingestion.

Design Overview (high level)

1) Runtime optimizations
- Kernel selection: Extend dynamic kernel selector to prefer low-precision fused kernels for eligible model layers.
- Batching profiles: New workload-aware default batching profiles for chat vs embedding workloads with adaptive batch caps.
- KV cache warm-start: Allow warm-start snapshots for long-running chat sessions to reduce cold-step latency.

2) Control plane and routing
- Cost-aware routing: Introduce routing policy that uses a weighted score of estimated token-cost, latency, and region preference.
- Fallbacks: Catalog of compatible model variants with ABI compatibility metadata for automatic fallback; compatibility table maintained in product metadata store.

3) Console & API changes
- Pricing API: Add /v2/pricing/estimate that returns token-cost estimates per-route and per-model variant.
- Console UX: Pricing comparison view between model variants and quantization profiles, with slider to simulate workload characteristics.

Design artifacts (examples)

- Pseudocode for cost-aware routing policy:

  score = w_cost * normalized_cost(model) + w_latency * predicted_latency(model) + w_region * region_penalty
  select model with min(score)

- Example CLI to snapshot warm KV cache:

  $ redwood runtime cache snapshot --session-id=abc123 --destination=s3://customer-kv-backups/session-abc123

Roadmap and Themes (Q4 2027 - Q1 2028)

Themes:
- Cost & Efficiency: Batching, quantization recommendations, and default profiles to reduce per-token costs.
- Reliability & Rollouts: Faster canaries, automated rollbacks, and Dedicated autoscaling improvements.
- Packaging & Clarity: Simplified pricing tiers and self-serve migration for SMB customers.

Milestones:
- 2027-10-15: Feature freeze for runtime changes targeting Q4 release.
- 2027-10-25: Begin customer canaries for pricing migration (opt-in).
- 2027-11-10: Public pricing & packaging announcement; docs and pricing API available.
- 2027-11-20: General availability for runtime improvements and console features.
- 2027-12-05: Dedicated autoscaling policy rollout complete for top-tier customers.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

Goals: simplify buying decisions, provide clearer trade-offs between Hosted and Dedicated, and introduce cost-based tooling to help customers choose model variants.

New packaging (summary):
- Developer (Hosted): usage-based, pay-as-you-go. Includes streaming, basic observability, 90-day migration guarantees.
- Growth (Hosted + Dedicated credits): discounted token pricing after spend threshold, basic reserved capacity.
- Enterprise (Dedicated & Private): committed monthly/annual contracts, SLA (99.95%), on-prem licensing, extended support.

Pricing rules & examples:
- Token pricing bands per model family (example):
  - small models (e.g., LLaMA-like quantized): $0.0004 / 1K prompt tokens, $0.0008 / 1K completion tokens
  - medium models: $0.0012 / 1K prompt tokens, $0.0024 / 1K completion tokens
  - large instruction models: $0.004 / 1K prompt tokens, $0.008 / 1K completion tokens

- Bundles: Growth tier includes $2,000 Dedicated credits per month (applied as first-dollar) and 15% discount on reserved capacity.
- Migration guarantees: Existing customers receive a 90-day billing safety window where they will not be charged more than their historical baseline without explicit opt-in.

Sales enablement & messaging:
- One-pager for sales with migration playbook, cost-savings calculators, and dedicated vs hosted decision tree.
- Competitive positioning: emphasize production economics, predictable latency, and unified tooling across environments.

Release Notes (Q4 2027 release)

Highlights:
- Unified pricing API (/v2/pricing/estimate) and new Console pricing comparison view.
- Runtime: workload-aware batching profiles and 15-30% average token-cost reduction on benchmark chat workloads.
- Rollouts: automatic fallback to compatible model variants and faster canary rollbacks.
- Dedicated: enhanced autoscaling policies and burst capacity for spike handling.

Breaking changes / migration notes:
- Pricing API v1 deprecated; v1 will be supported in read-only mode for 90 days. Customers must update to v2 for estimate features.
- Default batching behavior changed for applications that relied on unconstrained batch sizes; if you need prior behavior, set batching.max_batch_size to previous value in route config.

Operational runbook (summary)

- Canary rollout checklist:
  1. Create canary route with 2% traffic split.
  2. Monitor health metrics (errors, latency p95, token-cost variance) for 30 minutes.
  3. If any health policy breach, trigger automatic rollback and notify SRE oncall.

- Incident escalation thresholds:
  - Latency SLO breach: p95 > configured SLO for > 10 minutes -> P1 page and oncall.
  - Error rate spike: >1% client-facing error rate sustained for 5 minutes -> P1.

Metrics & Success Criteria

- Cost savings: median per-customer token-cost drop >= 20% for web chat workloads within three months.
- Adoption: 30% of paying customers opt into pricing migration or Growth tier within 90 days of GA.
- Reliability: rollback median time <30 minutes for Dedicated rollouts; canary rollback automation success >= 95%.

Appendix: Example route config (YAML)

  route_id: chat-default
  model_family: llama-3-quantized
  batching:
    strategy: adaptive
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_latency_ms: 200
  routing_policy: cost-aware
  autoscale:
    enabled: true
    scale_up_threshold_rps: 1200
    cooldown_seconds: 120

If you have questions or require a detailed walkthrough, contact the owners above or schedule a review with Product Engineering.
